It read my inbox and calendar, and it runs every weekday at seven. Here's the setup.
Step one. Connect Gmail and Google Calendar. In Claude, that's Customize, then Connectors.
Step two. Write the brief like you'd brief a person: today's meetings, emails that need me, and anything I promised someone.
Three sections, five lines each, and skip the newsletters.
Step three. Tell Claude: every weekday at seven, run this. Answer its questions, then hit Schedule.
It runs in the cloud, so your laptop can sleep too.
Step four. Read it with your coffee. Every run waits for you as its own session.
The clever part? Ask it to draft your replies. Sending still waits for your okay.
The catch. Scheduling needs a paid plan. It sees one Google account. It can't open attachments. And on work accounts, your admin has to switch it on.
